items.q: The resistance of a transformer winding is 0.5 ohms and it carries 5 A. Calculate the copper loss in watts.
items.s: Copper loss = I squared R = 5 x 5 x 0.5 = 12.5 W.

items.q: A transformer has a core loss of 800 W and a full load copper loss of 1200 W. Calculate its total loss at full load in watts.
items.s: Total loss = 800 + 1200 = 2000 W.

items.q: A three phase transformer bank is rated 30 kVA in total. Calculate the rating of each single phase unit in kilovolt amperes.
items.s: Per unit rating = 30/3 = 10 kVA.

items.q: A shunt generator supplies 220 V and its field circuit has a resistance of 250 ohms. Calculate the field current in amperes.
A series generator supplies a load current of 45 A. State the current flowing in its field winding in amperes.
items.s: In a series machine the field carries the whole load current, so If = Ia = 45 A.

items.q: A winding reaches a steady temperature of 80 degrees celsius in an ambient of 60 degrees celsius. Calculate its temperature rise in kelvin.
items.s: Temperature rise = 80 - 60 = 20 K.

items.q: A transformer with 500 primary turns and 200 secondary turns is supplied at 240 V. Calculate the secondary voltage in volts.
A transformer delivers 110 V from a secondary of 200 turns wound on a core whose primary has 1000 turns. Calculate the primary voltage in volts.
The primary of a transformer takes 50 A and has 1000 turns while the secondary has 50 turns. Calculate the secondary current in amperes.
A transformer is rated 3300 V on its secondary and delivers 100 A at full load. Calculate its rating in kilovolt amperes.
items.s: Rating = V I = 3300 x 100 = 330 kVA after dividing by 1000.

items.q: A transformer with a primary of 200 turns is to step 2400 V down to 415 V. Calculate the number of secondary turns required.
A transformer delivers 10 kW to its load while its total losses are 5 kW. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: Efficiency = output/(output + losses) x 100 = 10/(10 + 5) x 100 = 66.67%.

items.q: A transformer delivers 50 kW at an efficiency of 90 percent. Calculate the input power in kilowatts.
items.s: Input = output/(efficiency) = 50/0.9... = 50/0.9 = 55.56 kW.

items.q: A transformer has a core loss of 500 W and a full load copper loss of 2000 W. Calculate the per unit load at which maximum efficiency occurs.
items.s: Load = root of (core loss/full load copper loss) = root of (500/2000) = 0.5.

items.q: A transformer has a no load secondary voltage of 430 V and a full load secondary voltage of 415 V. Calculate its voltage regulation as a percentage.
Over one day a transformer delivers 480 kWh while the energy taken from the supply is 520 kWh. Calculate its all day efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: All day efficiency = 480/520 x 100 = 92.31%.

items.q: A transformer with an efficiency of 95 percent delivers 80 kW. Calculate its total loss in kilowatts.
A star connected transformer winding has a phase voltage of 3300 V. Calculate the line voltage in volts.
items.s: Line voltage = root 3 x phase voltage = 1.732 x 3300 = 5716 V.

items.q: A three phase supply has a line voltage of 440 V and the windings are star connected. Calculate the voltage across one winding in volts.
items.s: Phase voltage = line voltage/root 3 = 440/1.732 = 254 V.

items.q: A three phase transformer delivers 50 A per line at 415 V with a power factor of 0.9. Calculate the output power in kilowatts.
items.s: P = root 3 x VL x IL x cos(phi) = 1.732 x 415 x 50 x 0.9 = 32.35 kW.

items.q: A delta connected winding carries a line current of 50 A. Calculate the current in each phase winding in amperes.
items.s: Phase current = line current/root 3 = 50/1.732 = 28.87 A.

items.q: A 4 pole generator has 500 armature conductors, a flux of 0.03 Wb per pole and runs at 1000 rpm with 4 parallel paths. Calculate the generated emf in volts.
A 6 pole lap wound generator with 600 conductors develops 220 V at a flux of 0.02 Wb per pole. Calculate its speed in rpm.
A shunt generator delivers a line current of 50 A while its field takes 1 A. Calculate the armature current in amperes.
A dc motor is connected to 400 V, draws an armature current of 20 A and has an armature resistance of 0.2 ohms. Calculate the back emf in volts.
A 6 pole motor with 800 armature conductors and 2 parallel paths carries 30 A in a flux of 0.04 Wb per pole. Calculate the torque developed in newton metres.
A motor develops a back emf of 240 V while carrying an armature current of 40 A. Calculate the mechanical power developed in watts.
items.s: Pm = Eb x Ia = 240 x 40 = 9600 W.

items.q: A motor runs at 1440 rpm while developing 7500 W of mechanical power. Calculate the torque in newton metres.
A motor runs at 1200 rpm with a back emf of 230 V. Assuming the flux is unchanged, calculate its speed in rpm when the back emf falls to 180 V.
items.s: Speed is proportional to back emf, so n2 = n1 x Eb2/Eb1 = 1200 x 180/230 = 939.1 rpm.

items.q: A dc motor takes 20 A from a 220 V supply. Calculate the input power in kilowatts.
items.s: Input = V IL = 220 x 20 = 4.4 kW.

items.q: A motor takes 10 kW from the supply and its losses total 1 kW. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: Efficiency = (input - losses)/input x 100 = (10 - 1)/10 x 100 = 90%.

items.q: A motor runs at 1500 rpm with a flux of 0.03 Wb per pole. If field weakening reduces the flux to 0.015 Wb per pole, calculate the new speed in rpm.
items.s: Speed is inversely proportional to flux, so n2 = n1 x phi1/phi2 = 1500 x 0.03/0.015 = 3000 rpm.

items.q: A 220 V motor of armature resistance 1 ohms is to be started with the armature current limited to 40 A. Calculate the series starting resistance required in ohms.
items.s: R total = V/Ia = 220/40 = 5.5 ohms, so the added resistance is 4.5 ohms.

items.q: The armature of a shunt motor takes 50 A while the field takes 2.5 A. Calculate the line current in amperes.
A motor has a torque constant per unit current of 0.8 N m per A and is driven from 240 V. Calculate the no load speed in thousands of rpm if the torque is negligible.
items.s: At no load Eb is about equal to 240 V, so angular speed = 240/0.8 = 300 rad per second, which is 2865 rpm or 2.86 thousand rpm = 2.87.

items.q: In a no load test a machine takes 2 kW and its no load losses are 0.5 kW. Express the constant losses as a percentage of input.
items.s: Constant loss as a percentage of input = 0.5/2 x 100 = 25%.

items.q: In an open circuit test a transformer draws 1.5 A at 240 V with a power factor of 0.4. Calculate the core loss in watts.
items.s: Core loss = V I cos(phi) = 240 x 1.5 x 0.4 = 144 W.

items.q: In a short circuit test the applied voltage is 15 V while the current is 10 A. Calculate the copper loss in watts.
items.s: Copper loss = short circuit voltage x current = 15 x 10 = 150 W.

items.q: Two transformers of 200 kVA and 400 kVA share a total load of 300 kVA in proportion to their ratings. Calculate the load carried by the first unit in kilovolt amperes.
items.s: Load 1 = total x rating1/(sum of ratings) = 300 x 200/(200 + 400) = 100 kVA.

items.q: A transformer has 400 primary turns and 200 secondary turns. Calculate its turns ratio.
items.s: Turns ratio = N1/N2 = 400/200 = 2.

items.q: The resistance of a transformer winding is 1 ohms and it carries 25 A. Calculate the copper loss in watts.
items.s: Copper loss = I squared R = 25 x 25 x 1 = 625 W.

items.q: A transformer has a core loss of 600 W and a full load copper loss of 1200 W. Calculate its total loss at full load in watts.

items.q: The primary of a transformer takes 5 A and has 200 turns while the secondary has 200 turns. Calculate the secondary current in amperes.
A transformer delivers 50 kW at an efficiency of 96 percent. Calculate the input power in kilowatts.
items.s: Input = output/(efficiency) = 50/0.9... = 50/0.96 = 52.08 kW.

items.q: A transformer has a no load secondary voltage of 415 V and a full load secondary voltage of 240 V. Calculate its voltage regulation as a percentage.
A three phase transformer delivers 20 A per line at 415 V with a power factor of 0.85. Calculate the output power in kilowatts.
items.s: P = root 3 x VL x IL x cos(phi) = 1.732 x 415 x 20 x 0.85 = 12.22 kW.

items.q: A delta connected winding carries a line current of 20 A. Calculate the current in each phase winding in amperes.
items.s: Phase current = line current/root 3 = 20/1.732 = 11.55 A.

items.q: A dc motor is connected to 220 V, draws an armature current of 25 A and has an armature resistance of 0.5 ohms. Calculate the back emf in volts.
A motor runs at 1500 rpm while developing 3000 W of mechanical power. Calculate the torque in newton metres.
In an open circuit test a transformer draws 0.5 A at 400 V with a power factor of 0.3. Calculate the core loss in watts.
items.s: Core loss = V I cos(phi) = 400 x 0.5 x 0.3 = 60 W.

items.q: Two transformers of 300 kVA and 100 kVA share a total load of 150 kVA in proportion to their ratings. Calculate the load carried by the first unit in kilovolt amperes.
items.s: Load 1 = total x rating1/(sum of ratings) = 150 x 300/(300 + 100) = 112.5 kVA.

items.q: A transformer has 200 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Calculate its turns ratio.
items.s: Turns ratio = N1/N2 = 200/250 = 0.8.

items.q: A transformer with 200 primary turns and 50 secondary turns is supplied at 240 V. Calculate the secondary voltage in volts.
A transformer is rated 415 V on its secondary and delivers 100 A at full load. Calculate its rating in kilovolt amperes.
items.s: Rating = V I = 415 x 100 = 41.5 kVA after dividing by 1000.

items.q: A transformer with a primary of 1000 turns is to step 2400 V down to 240 V. Calculate the number of secondary turns required.
A transformer delivers 50 kW to its load while its total losses are 5 kW. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: Efficiency = output/(output + losses) x 100 = 50/(50 + 5) x 100 = 90.91%.

items.q: The resistance of a transformer winding is 1 ohms and it carries 10 A. Calculate the copper loss in watts.
items.s: Copper loss = I squared R = 10 x 10 x 1 = 100 W.

items.q: A transformer has a core loss of 800 W and a full load copper loss of 400 W. Calculate the per unit load at which maximum efficiency occurs.
items.s: Load = root of (core loss/full load copper loss) = root of (800/400) = 1.41.

items.q: Over one day a transformer delivers 600 kWh while the energy taken from the supply is 800 kWh. Calculate its all day efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: All day efficiency = 600/800 x 100 = 75%.

items.q: A three phase transformer bank is rated 60 kVA in total. Calculate the rating of each single phase unit in kilovolt amperes.
items.s: Per unit rating = 60/3 = 20 kVA.

items.q: A 2 pole generator has 600 armature conductors, a flux of 0.03 Wb per pole and runs at 1000 rpm with 2 parallel paths. Calculate the generated emf in volts.
A 6 pole lap wound generator with 800 conductors develops 220 V at a flux of 0.03 Wb per pole. Calculate its speed in rpm.
A shunt generator supplies 220 V and its field circuit has a resistance of 120 ohms. Calculate the field current in amperes.
A shunt generator delivers a line current of 60 A while its field takes 5 A. Calculate the armature current in amperes.
A 6 pole motor with 400 armature conductors and 2 parallel paths carries 40 A in a flux of 0.02 Wb per pole. Calculate the torque developed in newton metres.
A motor develops a back emf of 220 V while carrying an armature current of 40 A. Calculate the mechanical power developed in watts.
items.s: Pm = Eb x Ia = 220 x 40 = 8800 W.

items.q: A motor runs at 1500 rpm with a back emf of 230 V. Assuming the flux is unchanged, calculate its speed in rpm when the back emf falls to 210 V.
items.s: Speed is proportional to back emf, so n2 = n1 x Eb2/Eb1 = 1500 x 210/230 = 1370 rpm.

items.q: A motor runs at 1500 rpm with a flux of 0.02 Wb per pole. If field weakening reduces the flux to 0.015 Wb per pole, calculate the new speed in rpm.
items.s: Speed is inversely proportional to flux, so n2 = n1 x phi1/phi2 = 1500 x 0.02/0.015 = 2000 rpm.

items.q: A 240 V motor of armature resistance 0.2 ohms is to be started with the armature current limited to 40 A. Calculate the series starting resistance required in ohms.
items.s: R total = V/Ia = 240/40 = 6 ohms, so the added resistance is 5.8 ohms.

items.q: A motor has a torque constant per unit current of 1 N m per A and is driven from 240 V. Calculate the no load speed in thousands of rpm if the torque is negligible.
items.s: At no load Eb is about equal to 240 V, so angular speed = 240/1 = 240 rad per second, which is 2292 rpm or 2.29 thousand rpm.

items.q: In a short circuit test the applied voltage is 15 V while the current is 25 A. Calculate the copper loss in watts.
items.s: Copper loss = short circuit voltage x current = 15 x 25 = 375 W.

items.q: A winding reaches a steady temperature of 75 degrees celsius in an ambient of 60 degrees celsius. Calculate its temperature rise in kelvin.
items.s: Temperature rise = 75 - 60 = 15 K.

items.q: A transformer has a no load secondary voltage of 250 V and a full load secondary voltage of 240 V. Calculate its voltage regulation as a percentage.

A motor takes 50 kW from the supply and its losses total 1 kW. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: Efficiency = (input - losses)/input x 100 = (50 - 1)/50 x 100 = 98%.

items.q: In an open circuit test a transformer draws 0.5 A at 240 V with a power factor of 0.3. Calculate the core loss in watts.

items.q: Two transformers of 300 kVA and 200 kVA share a total load of 300 kVA in proportion to their ratings. Calculate the load carried by the first unit in kilovolt amperes.

items.q: A transformer has a core loss of 200 W and a full load copper loss of 500 W. Calculate its total loss at full load in watts.

items.q: A transformer has a core loss of 400 W and a full load copper loss of 2000 W. Calculate the per unit load at which maximum efficiency occurs.

items.q: A transformer has a core loss of 500 W and a full load copper loss of 400 W. Calculate the per unit load at which maximum efficiency occurs.
items.s: Load = root of (core loss/full load copper loss) = root of (500/400) = 1.12.

items.q: A 2 pole generator has 800 armature conductors, a flux of 0.05 Wb per pole and runs at 1500 rpm with 2 parallel paths. Calculate the generated emf in volts.
A 6 pole lap wound generator with 800 conductors develops 400 V at a flux of 0.03 Wb per pole. Calculate its speed in rpm.
A 2 pole motor with 400 armature conductors and 2 parallel paths carries 50 A in a flux of 0.04 Wb per pole. Calculate the torque developed in newton metres.
A motor runs at 1000 rpm with a back emf of 220 V. Assuming the flux is unchanged, calculate its speed in rpm when the back emf falls to 200 V.
items.s: Speed is proportional to back emf, so n2 = n1 x Eb2/Eb1 = 1000 x 200/220 = 909.1 rpm.

items.q: A motor runs at 1800 rpm with a flux of 0.04 Wb per pole. If field weakening reduces the flux to 0.02 Wb per pole, calculate the new speed in rpm.
items.s: Speed is inversely proportional to flux, so n2 = n1 x phi1/phi2 = 1800 x 0.04/0.02 = 3600 rpm.

items.q: A 400 V motor of armature resistance 0.5 ohms is to be started with the armature current limited to 25 A. Calculate the series starting resistance required in ohms.
items.s: R total = V/Ia = 400/25 = 16 ohms, so the added resistance is 15.5 ohms.

items.q: A motor has a torque constant per unit current of 1.2 N m per A and is driven from 240 V. Calculate the no load speed in thousands of rpm if the torque is negligible.
items.s: At no load Eb is about equal to 240 V, so angular speed = 240/1.2 = 200 rad per second, which is 1910 rpm or 1.91 thousand rpm.

items.q: A transformer with 1000 primary turns and 200 secondary turns is supplied at 2400 V. Calculate the secondary voltage in volts.
A transformer delivers 415 V from a secondary of 250 turns wound on a core whose primary has 2000 turns. Calculate the primary voltage in volts.
The primary of a transformer takes 20 A and has 200 turns while the secondary has 50 turns. Calculate the secondary current in amperes.
A transformer delivers 20 kW to its load while its total losses are 0.5 kW. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: Efficiency = output/(output + losses) x 100 = 20/(20 + 0.5) x 100 = 97.56%.

items.q: A transformer has a core loss of 600 W and a full load copper loss of 500 W. Calculate its total loss at full load in watts.
items.s: Total loss = 600 + 500 = 1100 W.

items.q: A transformer has a no load secondary voltage of 240 V and a full load secondary voltage of 230 V. Calculate its voltage regulation as a percentage.
A transformer with an efficiency of 96 percent delivers 50 kW. Calculate its total loss in kilowatts.
A dc motor is connected to 110 V, draws an armature current of 10 A and has an armature resistance of 0.5 ohms. Calculate the back emf in volts.
A motor develops a back emf of 220 V while carrying an armature current of 20 A. Calculate the mechanical power developed in watts.
items.s: Pm = Eb x Ia = 220 x 20 = 4400 W.

items.q: A dc motor takes 50 A from a 400 V supply. Calculate the input power in kilowatts.
items.s: Input = V IL = 400 x 50 = 20 kW.

items.q: A motor takes 20 kW from the supply and its losses total 5 kW. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: Efficiency = (input - losses)/input x 100 = (20 - 5)/20 x 100 = 75%.

items.q: In a no load test a machine takes 6 kW and its no load losses are 0.4 kW. Express the constant losses as a percentage of input.
items.s: Constant loss as a percentage of input = 0.4/6 x 100 = 6.67%.

items.q: In an open circuit test a transformer draws 0.5 A at 220 V with a power factor of 0.3. Calculate the core loss in watts.
items.s: Core loss = V I cos(phi) = 220 x 0.5 x 0.3 = 33 W.

items.q: In a short circuit test the applied voltage is 20 V while the current is 25 A. Calculate the copper loss in watts.
items.s: Copper loss = short circuit voltage x current = 20 x 25 = 500 W.

items.q: A winding reaches a steady temperature of 80 degrees celsius in an ambient of 30 degrees celsius. Calculate its temperature rise in kelvin.
items.s: Temperature rise = 80 - 30 = 50 K.

items.q: Two transformers of 200 kVA and 100 kVA share a total load of 300 kVA in proportion to their ratings. Calculate the load carried by the first unit in kilovolt amperes.
items.s: Load 1 = total x rating1/(sum of ratings) = 300 x 200/(200 + 100) = 200 kVA.

items.q: A transformer with a primary of 200 turns is to step 240 V down to 240 V. Calculate the number of secondary turns required.
Over one day a transformer delivers 600 kWh while the energy taken from the supply is 520 kWh. Calculate its all day efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: All day efficiency = 600/520 x 100 = 115.4%.

items.q: A 2 pole generator has 800 armature conductors, a flux of 0.02 Wb per pole and runs at 1000 rpm with 4 parallel paths. Calculate the generated emf in volts.
A 4 pole lap wound generator with 800 conductors develops 220 V at a flux of 0.02 Wb per pole. Calculate its speed in rpm.
A 6 pole motor with 400 armature conductors and 2 parallel paths carries 30 A in a flux of 0.03 Wb per pole. Calculate the torque developed in newton metres.
A motor runs at 1500 rpm with a back emf of 230 V. Assuming the flux is unchanged, calculate its speed in rpm when the back emf falls to 200 V.
items.s: Speed is proportional to back emf, so n2 = n1 x Eb2/Eb1 = 1500 x 200/230 = 1304 rpm.

items.q: A motor runs at 1500 rpm with a flux of 0.02 Wb per pole. If field weakening reduces the flux to 0.01 Wb per pole, calculate the new speed in rpm.
items.s: Speed is inversely proportional to flux, so n2 = n1 x phi1/phi2 = 1500 x 0.02/0.01 = 3000 rpm.

items.q: A motor has a torque constant per unit current of 1.2 N m per A and is driven from 220 V. Calculate the no load speed in thousands of rpm if the torque is negligible.
items.s: At no load Eb is about equal to 220 V, so angular speed = 220/1.2 = 183.3 rad per second, which is 1751 rpm or 1.75 thousand rpm.

items.q: A transformer has 1000 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Calculate its turns ratio.
items.s: Turns ratio = N1/N2 = 1000/250 = 4.

items.q: A transformer with 500 primary turns and 50 secondary turns is supplied at 240 V. Calculate the secondary voltage in volts.
A transformer delivers 240 V from a secondary of 100 turns wound on a core whose primary has 1000 turns. Calculate the primary voltage in volts.
The primary of a transformer takes 5 A and has 200 turns while the secondary has 250 turns. Calculate the secondary current in amperes.
A transformer is rated 415 V on its secondary and delivers 50 A at full load. Calculate its rating in kilovolt amperes.
items.s: Rating = V I = 415 x 50 = 20.75 kVA after dividing by 1000.

items.q: A transformer delivers 100 kW to its load while its total losses are 2 kW. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: Efficiency = output/(output + losses) x 100 = 100/(100 + 2) x 100 = 98.04%.

items.q: The resistance of a transformer winding is 0.1 ohms and it carries 10 A. Calculate the copper loss in watts.
items.s: Copper loss = I squared R = 10 x 10 x 0.1 = 10 W.

items.q: A transformer delivers 75 kW at an efficiency of 90 percent. Calculate the input power in kilowatts.
items.s: Input = output/(efficiency) = 75/0.9... = 75/0.9 = 83.33 kW.

items.q: A transformer has a no load secondary voltage of 415 V and a full load secondary voltage of 230 V. Calculate its voltage regulation as a percentage.
A transformer with an efficiency of 95 percent delivers 40 kW. Calculate its total loss in kilowatts.
A star connected transformer winding has a phase voltage of 240 V. Calculate the line voltage in volts.
items.s: Line voltage = root 3 x phase voltage = 1.732 x 240 = 415.7 V.

items.q: A three phase transformer delivers 50 A per line at 415 V with a power factor of 0.8. Calculate the output power in kilowatts.
items.s: P = root 3 x VL x IL x cos(phi) = 1.732 x 415 x 50 x 0.8 = 28.75 kW.

items.q: A delta connected winding carries a line current of 30 A. Calculate the current in each phase winding in amperes.
items.s: Phase current = line current/root 3 = 30/1.732 = 17.32 A.

items.q: A shunt generator supplies 240 V and its field circuit has a resistance of 120 ohms. Calculate the field current in amperes.
A shunt generator delivers a line current of 50 A while its field takes 2.5 A. Calculate the armature current in amperes.
A dc motor is connected to 110 V, draws an armature current of 10 A and has an armature resistance of 0.4 ohms. Calculate the back emf in volts.
A motor takes 20 kW from the supply and its losses total 1 kW. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
items.s: Efficiency = (input - losses)/input x 100 = (20 - 1)/20 x 100 = 95%.

items.q: In a no load test a machine takes 3 kW and its no load losses are 0.5 kW. Express the constant losses as a percentage of input.
items.s: Constant loss as a percentage of input = 0.5/3 x 100 = 16.67%.

items.q: A winding reaches a steady temperature of 80 degrees celsius in an ambient of 40 degrees celsius. Calculate its temperature rise in kelvin.
items.s: Temperature rise = 80 - 40 = 40 K.

items.q: Two transformers of 200 kVA and 200 kVA share a total load of 150 kVA in proportion to their ratings. Calculate the load carried by the first unit in kilovolt amperes.

items.q: A transformer with a primary of 200 turns is to step 240 V down to 110 V. Calculate the number of secondary turns required.
